claims.claim: Corpus acquisition yielded 456 unique works via cursor pagination and exact deduplication.
Metadata completeness was assessed for ten fields.
The stated field-specific metadata coverage values are correct.
The corpus spans 2018–2023, grows from 1 to 190 works, and has CAGR 185.6%.
The trajectory is hyper-exponential.
Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences lead productivity.
Bradford-zone counts, citation statistics, and the leading cited works are correct.
The coauthorship network has 60 displayed nodes, 127 edges, and 10 communities, with Hou, Cao, and Hsieh prominent.
The institution network has 71 displayed nodes, 138 edges, and 10 communities, led by the two Chinese Academy institutions.
Collaboration is strongly intra-national and largely bounded within China.
The keyword network has 72 displayed nodes, 198 edges, and 7 communities led by computer-science terms.
Drug discovery, bioinformatics, and chemistry form a biomedical-application periphery around a computational core.
Bibliographic coupling delineates four substantive intellectual streams.
Cocitation confirms a foundation anchored by seminal GNN and molecular-featurization papers.
The research front is diversifying into geometry-enhanced, self-supervised, and interpretable architectures.
Association-strength normalization, Louvain clustering, deterministic layouts, and edge reduction were used.
Single-source, citation-window, document-type, abstract-missingness, and network-parameter caveats are acknowledged.
The study used 652 Web of Science Core Collection papers from 2017–2023 and Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace.
The search retrieved 843 candidates and manual title/abstract screening retained 652 records.
The corpus has 168 sources, 2,654 authors, and annual growth rate 149.8%.
Annual output was 1 in 2017 and 2018 and reached 243 in 2023.
China leads country output with 426 papers, followed by the United States with 142.
China and the United States hold leading positions and collaborate closely, while broader cooperation should improve.
The Chinese Academy of Sciences leads institutions with 39 papers, and the listed top institutions are Chinese.
Briefings in Bioinformatics leads journal output with 75 papers, while Bioinformatics has the highest total citations.
You Zhu-Hong, Deng Lei, and Zheng Mingyue are the three most productive authors.
The top-cited papers are Zitnik 2018, Altae-Tran 2017, and Xiong 2020.
Citation thresholds and TC/TP reflect research quality and impact.
China's lower average citations than the United States are caused by later entry and a shorter citation window.
Keywords identify DTI, drug repurposing, and drug–drug interaction as applications and graph convolutional methods as core algorithms.
Data availability, ethics, computing-resource balance, and interpretability are key technical challenges.
The field is at a high-growth stage with broad prospects and good development.

rationale: B is more consistently grounded in its paired article evidence and covers the major empirical dimensions, despite weak caution around citation-quality inference. A is more methodologically explicit but adds numerous unsupported claims about national boundedness, substantive intellectual streams, thematic peripheries, and architectural diversification.

claims.claim: Corpus acquisition yielded 259 unique works via cursor pagination and exact deduplication.
Metadata completeness values for 11 fields are correctly reported.
The corpus spans 2015–2022, rises from 2 to 72 works, and has endpoint CAGR 66.85%.
Citation mean is 72.09, median 32, zero-cited share 13.51%, and maximum 1,436.
Xiaohui Chen leads authors; Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen each lead institutions.
International Journal of Molecular Sciences leads sources and Bradford Zone 1 has 23 sources and 85 documents.
The five network sizes and cluster counts match the canonical outputs.
The principal keyword trajectories are reported correctly.
The 66.85% CAGR substantially exceeds typical established biomedical-field growth.
The 2022 output concentration demonstrates accelerating translational momentum.
The mean-to-median citation ratio shows foundational methodologies concentrate impact.
Eleven of the top fifteen institutions are Chinese.
Keyword clusters form a translational pipeline from EV characterization to clinical delivery.
The coupling network establishes EV-mediated CRISPR delivery as the central integrating theme.
The field progressed through three chronological stages ending in therapeutic applications.
Single-source, citation-window, metadata, document-type, and network-parameter limitations are acknowledged.
The study used 219 WoSCC records on CRISPR-related extracellular-vesicle research from 2015–2022.
The final corpus followed screening from 231 records and contains 164 articles and 55 reviews.
R, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and GraphPad Prism were used.
Annual output rose over the period and relative research interest was analyzed.
China leads publication count; the United States leads total citations and H-index; Canada leads average citations.
Wang Y. and Zhang H. each published six papers, while Zhao X.X. has the highest average citations among the top six.
The analysis identifies 141 core authors and 31 countries for collaboration mapping.
The USA, England, Germany, China, and Canada lead country collaboration link strength.
The collaboration maps establish a domestic-partner preference and geographic restriction.
Nature, PNAS, and Nature Communications are the three most cocited journals.
The reference cocitation map has three clusters covering CRISPR/Cas, EV delivery, and EV-characterization reviews.
The keyword analysis uses 317 keywords occurring at least twice and identifies seven clusters.
Expression, cells, Cas9, RNA, CRISPR/Cas9, cancer, and exosome are leading keywords.
The literature evolved from mechanism and target studies in 2015–2020 toward delivery, gene therapy, nanomaterials, and translation in 2020–2022.
Citation bursts directly measure popularity and research quality.

rationale: B is more consistently supported by its paired article evidence and provides broad coverage of growth, geography, collaboration, cocitation, and keyword evolution. A offers better reproducibility but repeatedly converts descriptive trends and network layouts into unsupported field-maturity, impact, translational-stage, and intellectual-centrality claims.
